summary: Verified the 3 pending HeartLink features end-to-end on the public preview URL. (1) Show-password toggles on login+signup: PASS. (2) Chat filter (Recent/Oldest/Unread) on Messages tab: PASS - pills render, active state highlights, ordering verified with 2 seeded conversations. (3) badge_update WebSocket: PASS - verified over a real WS connection (badge increments on new message, unread cleared after mark-read) and in the UI navbar (Chats badge 2->3 on live incoming message, back to 2 after opening chat). Login flow with admin credentials reaches /discover. Backend: 10 passed, 1 skipped (no badge-counts REST endpoint). Found 3 non-blocking defects (404 prefetch endpoint, stale matches cache, Alerts badge double-counting).

minor.issue: Endpoint does not exist (404). frontend/src/utils/cacheManager.js:70 prefetchRecentChats() calls it on every app load -> 2 console 404 errors per session and chat prefetch/cache never works. Either add the endpoint or point prefetch at /api/matches/{user_id} + /api/messages/{match_id}/last.

matches_cache (TTLCache ttl=120s, database.py:39) is never invalidated when a new match is created (server.py ~3300 mutual-like path). Reproduced: mutual like returned {action: matched, match_id: ...} but GET /api/matches/{user_id} kept returning the old list for ~2 min, so a brand-new match / its chat is invisible to the user for up to 2 minutes.

send_badge_update is only fired when modified_count > 0 (server.py:3890-3904). If a client badge is stale but nothing needs updating, the badge never self-heals. Consider always sending the badge update.

ui_bugs.issue: Alerts badge = notification_count + unread_messages (Navbar.jsx:34) while each new message ALSO creates an in-app notification, so one incoming message increments Alerts by 2 (observed 14 -> 16) and only drops by 1 after reading (16 -> 15). Double counting makes the Alerts badge permanently inflated.

Visiting /matches or /chat/* hard-resets unreadMessages to 0 locally (Navbar.jsx:29) even when other conversations still have unread messages; the correct count only reappears after the next badge_update or page reload.

integration_issues.issue: prefetchRecentChats hits non-existent /api/matches/{id}/conversations -> 404 console errors, silent failure (caught by empty catch)

issues: No issues: pills have adequate contrast (active = #D6336C on white text), correct spacing above the list
'Unread' pill only re-sorts by unread count; read conversations are still listed. Label suggests filtering - consider renaming to 'Unread first' or actually filtering (product decision)
Unlabeled '50' chip at top-left overlaps the card header area - unclear meaning to users
Users without photos render a giant single-letter placeholder ('F') filling the whole card

action_items: Fix cacheManager.prefetchRecentChats to use existing endpoints (or add GET /api/matches/{user_id}/conversations) - currently 404 on every load
Invalidate matches_cache for both users when a new match is created (mutual-like path) so new matches appear immediately
Stop double-counting unread messages in the Alerts badge (Navbar.jsx:34) since messages also create in-app notifications
Optional: always send badge_update from mark-read even when modified_count == 0
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 7663 lines - should be split into routers (auth/matches/messages/admin) per the 700-line guideline
GET /api/matches caches results for 120s with no write-through invalidation on match creation; any endpoint that mutates db.matches should pop matches_cache for both user ids
MatchesPage.fetchConversations issues 2 extra HTTP calls per match (last + unread-count) in a Promise.all fan-out; a single aggregated conversations endpoint would cut N*2 requests

success_rate.frontend: 100% of the 3 requested features pass; 3 unrelated defects found

rca_of_the_issue: All 3 features were implemented correctly. The 404s in console come from cacheManager.js:70 calling a route that was never implemented in server.py; the 'new match not visible' behaviour is the un-invalidated 120s matches_cache; the inflated Alerts badge comes from summing notification_count + unread_messages while message events also create in-app notifications.
